text:
lena.sales: FYI Acme POC hit a confusing 401/403 mix during a demo. They reported intermittent failures after key rotation. Can we triage? @chris.support @arun.eng

chris.support: Got it. Any error bodies from the API? 401 vs 403 usually means auth vs authz.

lena.sales: Paste from customer: `HTTP/1.1 403 Forbidden` ``{"error":"forbidden","reason":"project_mismatch"}`` then later `401 {"error":"invalid_token"}`. They think the SDK is flapping.

arun.eng: Two quick checks: 1) Which token are they using (project-scoped vs org-scoped)? 2) Are they setting X-Redwood-Project or X-Redwood-Org headers in their proxy?

acme-dev: customer: We rotate keys nightly via CI. Our frontend sets `X-Redwood-Project: proj-456` because the old docs had examples. We switched the token but maybe the header stayed.

chris.support: That header can override the token's bound project and cause project_mismatch if token is for proj-789. Can you run the introspect endpoint and paste redacted output? Example: `curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/oauth/introspect -d "token=SK_live_..." -u client:secret`

arun.eng: Also check token created_at vs rotation window. If the token was invalidated/rotated in-between you'll see `active:false` in introspect which explains the 401.

acme-dev: Here's introspect (redacted): `{"active": true, "org_id": "org-A", "project_id": "proj-789", "scopes":["inference:generate"]}`

chris.support: So token is active and bound to proj-789. But frontend header says proj-456 -> project_mismatch 403. The 401s might be from calls to the embed endpoint using an expired token from an older service. Do they use multiple tokens?

acme-dev: We have a background job issuing short-lived tokens for service B. Maybe that one didn't rotate properly.

arun.eng: Remediation steps: 1) Remove X-Redwood-Project/X-Redwood-Org headers unless you need cross-org calls. 2) Ensure CI writes a single canonical token to all services. 3) If you need header override, use tokens with matching project scope.

nina.sec: Also check audit logs: who issued token and whether the old token was revoked. We can provide a short script to search audit events for token rotations.

chris.support: Sent a minimal test to the customer to reproduce: `curl -H "Authorization: Bearer SK_live_NEW" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/health` and `curl -H "Authorization: Bearer SK_live_NEW" -H "X-Redwood-Project: proj-456" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -d '{"input":"test"}'` should show 200 and 403 respectively.

acme-dev: Ran those exactly. Health check 200. Generate without header -> 200. Generate with header -> 403 project_mismatch.

arun.eng: Good repro. I'm going to add a hint in our error payload to include expected token binding (sanitized) so customer sees which project/org the token is bound to. Filing ENG-891.

infra-bot: Deployed a proxy rule to log incoming X-Redwood-Org/Project headers for the next 24h for POC customer traffic (trace id: p-8901).

chris.support: For immediate unblock, instructed them to remove the header and rollout the new token to all services. Also asked them to add a CI check that fails if mismatch is detected in health smoke tests.

lena.sales: Customer confirmed removing header fixed flapping during the demo. They're asking for a short KB on "common auth pitfalls during key rotation" + a mention in the onboarding quickstart. Can docs own a one-paragraph note?

nina.sec: I'll approve wording; include a note about short-lived tokens, rotation cadence, and auditing. Also recommend using the SDK which auto-omits header overrides by default.

acme-dev: Thanks team. We'll also switch to org-scoped token for dashboard services and project-scoped for per-project workers.

chris.support: Closing the immediate swarm. Follow-ups: ENG-891 (improve error hints), DOCS-452 (KB), and SEC-230 (rotation audit template). Owner: chris.support.

lena.sales: Great, I'll log this in the deal notes and set expectation for a one-off integration fee for extra SRE handholding during go-live. :white_check_mark:
